versionRationale: Authored deterministic capacity corpus. Counts and outcomes derive from existing contracts, not response snapshots. Q1 defines 64 MiB TXT ingest as sixteen sequential 4 MiB documents. Digest changes require a new version and behavioral rationale. Version 1.1.0 binds large prefilter to the existing QueryGrant maximum of 4096 allowed source versions over the unchanged 10000-source/100000-chunk corpus; a 4097-entry grant must fail. The reference corpus alternates equal-byte EN and RU texts and preserves exact IR/span digests. Version 1.2.0 adds query-plan counterfactuals after full-scale loading exposed tenant scans in exact block and snapshot-member guards. Additive migration 012 indexes the existing predicates without changing their semantics. Version 1.3.0 binds a valid reference index manifest above 1 MiB to the existing 16 MiB schema ceiling, and adds the above-16-MiB negative boundary. The generic JSON default was not the approved index-manifest contract. Version 1.4.0 removes only a redundant legacy 4 MiB persistence guard discovered on full manifest sealing; the existing 16 MiB SQL guard remains. Positive SQL above 4 MiB and negative SQL above 16 MiB test the same approved wire ceiling. Version 1.5.0 adds changed-bytes/digest and post-cache committed-revoke negatives after the fixed 20-client workload measured warm p95 above the unchanged 500 ms target. A single-entry immutable validation cache preserves authoritative per-request checks. Version 1.5.1 qualifies optional cgroup diagnostics for absent leaf controllers, inherited quotas and namespace mount roots; workload sizes, golden outcomes, SLOs and hardware qualification requirements are unchanged. The load actor IPC frame now accepts the existing serialized search configuration above 1 MiB under an explicit 16 MiB ceiling, rejecting truncated or oversized frames without changing the product limits. Runtime build scripts and the worker lockfile are now measurement fingerprints, and real OCR runs require matching runtime build provenance, so changed sandbox/dependency inputs invalidate earlier observations rather than reusing stale evidence. Qualified dependency upgrade to Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Torchvision 0.28.0+cpu and pypdfium2 5.15.2 changes parser identity only: all 12 PDF/OCR IR semantics were independently equal, and fresh sandbox plus PHP persistence validated the new identities. Rebind cross-suite references without changing authored workload or outcome expectations.
origin: Project-authored TXT generator and synthetic catalog identities; existing project-authored retrieval/scanned PDF fixtures bound by the group manifest.
